question.problem:
| $f(x,y)$ | $Y=-1$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | ${f}_{X}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=-2$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.2$ | $0.5$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.1$ | $0$ | $0.4$ | $0.5$ |
| ${f}_{Y}$ | $0.2$ | $0.2$ | $0.6$ | $1$ |

The joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ is shown above. Given that 

$$
\text{E}[X]=0,\,\text{E}[Y]=0.4,\,\text{SD}[X]=2,\,\text{SD}[Y]=0.8,
$$

 
find the correlation coefficient of $X$ and $Y.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the correlation coefficient of random variables $X$ and $Y$ is defined as

$$
\rho =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[Y]},
$$

where

- $\text{Cov}[X,Y]$ is the covariance, and

- $\text{SD}[X]$ and $\text{SD}[Y]$ are the standard deviations of $X$ and $Y.$

First, by applying the rule of the lazy statistician, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{X}}{\sum }_{y\in {S}_{Y}}xy\,f(x,y) \\  & =(-2)\cdot (-1)\cdot 0.1+(-2)\cdot 0\cdot 0.2+(-2)\cdot 1\cdot 0.2 \\  & +2\cdot (-1)\cdot 0.1+2\cdot 0\cdot 0+2\cdot 1\cdot 0.4 \\  & =0.4.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the covariance and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =0.4-(0)(0.4) \\  & =0.4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correlation coefficient is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\rho  & =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[Y]} \\  & =\frac{0.4}{2\cdot 0.8} \\  & =0.25.\end{aligned}
$$
